fantrax_getdraftpicks_completed_snake_em.note: The first real getDraftPicks response this project has ever received. League b2gyornvms4606iv held a COMPLETED 18-round 12-team snake draft (216 picks) at capture time; the endpoint returned an empty list anyway. Unauthenticated: no userSecretId was sent. The list key is 'currentDraftPicks', which was not among the parser's guesses ('draftPicks', 'picks'). Byte-exact, 24 bytes, no trailing newline.

fantrax_getleagueinfo_settings_sanitized.note: Identity-bearing sections were removed whole. No retained source value was edited. The 2026-09-05 response added the retained top-level playoffs object. The endpoint succeeded without userSecretId.

fantrax_getplayerids_nba.json.note: Committed in full. The whole point of this fixture is the row mix — player rows alongside the 30 team entities that risk R24 is about — so trimming it would remove the thing it exists to test.

nba_commonallplayers_current.json.note: Current-season rosters, which is what the crosswalk must match against. Matching against a historical season manufactures a team disagreement for every player who moved in the offseason.

nba_injury_report_2025-11-01_0530pm.pdf.note: Real captured report, committed whole rather than trimmed: it is a 7-page PDF (~79KB) and the parser's row-boundary logic depends on the full multi-page, multi-matchup, multi-line-reason and page-footer structure, including a same-team 'NOT YET SUBMITTED' marker row for two teams whose report had not been filed as of this capture.

nba_leaguegamefinder_cohort_window_2025_.note: Whole real rows/objects retained for six named games spanning both window boundaries and the two neutral-site 2025-12-13 games. No value edited. Rows are regrouped so each game's two rows are adjacent and games appear in the order named above; the row set is identical to the source's, only its order differs, and the parser is order-independent by construction (a contract test reverses the row set and asserts the same result). Verified 2026-08-20: the source's own row order is NOT stable across requests -- two captures minutes apart returned the same twelve rows in a different order -- so a byte diff between re-recordings of this fixture is expected and is not evidence the payload changed.

nba_leaguegamefinder_playoffs.json.note: Whole real rows retained as complete playoff game groups. No value edited.

nba_leaguegamefinder_reconciliation.json.note: Whole real rows retained for one ordinary reciprocal game and one game where both team rows repeat the same canonical MATCHUP. No value edited.

nba_leaguegamefinder_trimmed.json.note: Whole rows removed; only complete two-row game groups are retained. Required cross-endpoint game 0022400306 is included. No value edited.

nba_player_movement.json.gz.note: Complete response body, losslessly compressed without parsing or re-serialization. Includes player rows and consideration-only trade rows.

nba_playergamelogs_cohort_window_2025_26.note: Whole real rows/objects retained for six named games spanning both window boundaries and the two neutral-site 2025-12-13 games. No value edited. This endpoint carries its own GAME_DATE, which is what makes it an independent witness to the window rather than a restatement of the schedule query.

nba_playergamelogs_trimmed.json.note: Whole rows removed from the end. No value edited.

nba_playerindex_current.json.note: The listed NBA position for every player, one row per person id. This is the only position source this project has: BoxScoreTraditionalV3.position is a starting-lineup slot (five per team per game, F,F,C,G,G), not a player attribute. Untrimmed on purpose - the contract test asserts on coverage and on the position vocabulary across the whole league, and both assertions are meaningless over an arbitrary prefix of the rows.

nba_scheduleleaguev2_2026_27.json.note: Recorded slice preserves resolved games, two source-declared pending NBA Cup games, and October/March time-zone transitions. Source has 1,206 regular-season entries: 1,200 resolved games plus six pending. Field-trimmed as well as date-trimmed -- each game object retains only gameId, gameDateTimeEst, gameDateTimeUTC, gameLabel, homeTeam and awayTeam, and each team block only teamId/teamName/teamCity/teamTricode (no teamSlug). Re-verified against a fresh live capture on 2026-08-20T21:35Z: all 12 games still present and every retained field byte-identical, including both pending team blocks. See nba_scheduleleaguev2_2026_27_pending_knockout.json for a whole-object slice.

nba_scheduleleaguev2_2026_27_pending_kno.note: Whole, unmodified game objects -- unlike nba_scheduleleaguev2_2026_27.json above, which is field-trimmed and therefore cannot show what the source actually publishes for a team whose identity is undecided. Kept for ADR-013: every one of the six pending games in the 2026-27 season is here (0022601201-04 quarterfinals on 12/04 and 12/05, 0022601229-30 semifinals on 12/08), alongside 18 resolved games from opening night and the final regular-season date. A pending team block reads {teamId: 0, teamName: null, teamCity: null, teamTricode: null, teamSlug: null} with gameStatusText 'TBD', gameLabel 'Emirates NBA Cup', gameSubLabel 'Quarterfinal'/'Semifinal', gameSubtype 'in-season-knockout' and seriesText 'Date subject to change'. That every naming field is null, and not merely the id zero, is what makes the pending/failure distinction determinable from the payload rather than inferred. Whole-season aggregate at capture time: 1,206 source entries = 1,200 resolved + 6 pending, 30 teams at exactly 80 games each, 2026-10-20 to 2027-04-11.

nba_scheduleleaguev2_2026_27_gamedates.j.note: A dates-only calendar, not a trimmed slice of game objects like nba_scheduleleaguev2_2026_27.json above: every gameDate is kept, but each is reduced to just its date string, with no game/team/player identities. Built for the injury-report current-season live-smoke probe (test_live_smoke.py::TestInjuryReportCurrentSeasonIsAlive) to select a recent, independently game-backed candidate date without guessing a calendar date has a game -- the three sparse anchors in nba_scheduleleaguev2_2026_27.json produced gaps up to ~100 days, far too coarse for that purpose. The 13 preseason-only dates (every game that day labelled gameLabel == 'Preseason') are deliberately excluded: the injury-report adapter is out of scope before the season's first game (R40, docs/backlog.md). The largest gap among the 160 kept regular-season dates is 7 days (2027-02-18 -> 2027-02-25, the All-Star break).

nba_scheduleleaguev2_cohort_window_2025_.note: Whole real rows/objects retained for six named games spanning both window boundaries and the two neutral-site 2025-12-13 games. No value edited. Only the gameDates entries holding the named games are retained, and within each retained entry only the named games -- 2025-12-08 had a full slate and appears here with one game. Each retained game object is the source's own, unmodified.

nba_static_teams.json.note: Packaged with nba_api; no network call.

nba_injury_report_2024-01-10_0530pm.pdf.note: Real captured 2023-24 report, committed whole. One of three season fixtures pinning that the historical sweep's planned seasons still parse; this is the oldest season this project's parser can read. Carries both scarce designations (3 probable, 3 doubtful), which is the point: secondary sources claim the NBA vocabulary has no PROBABLE at all, and if that were true a multi-season sweep would leave injury-status-conversion unactivatable on probable. Retrieval evidence, including this response's SHA-256, is in docs/adapters/nba-injury-report-archive-reach-probe.json.

nba_injury_report_2025-01-15_0530pm.pdf.note: Real captured 2024-25 report, committed whole. Second of three season fixtures for the historical sweep. Carries 13 probable and 5 doubtful designations - the densest rare-status capture of the probe, and the direct falsification of the claim that PROBABLE is absent from the pre-2025-26 vocabulary. Retrieval evidence in docs/adapters/nba-injury-report-archive-reach-probe.json.

nba_injury_report_2023-01-11_0530pm_unsu.note: Real captured 2022-23 report in the pre-2023 word-spacing layout, committed whole and committed deliberately as a fixture the parser MUST REFUSE. It fetches cleanly - HTTP 200, valid PDF magic, five pages of genuine injury data with real players, matchups and designations - so nothing in transport notices anything wrong, and only the parser stands between this layout and a cohort of plausible nonsense. The archive reaches back to at least 2019-20 in this layout; the boundary at which this project's parser stops working is bracketed between 2023-04-05 (refused) and 2023-10-25 (parsed). Retrieval evidence in docs/adapters/nba-injury-report-archive-reach-probe.json.
